response.consequence: When embedding is on (`__rest_serializer === "1"`), a null `*_ids` field throws and the model fails to load. An unresolved id yields a `colors` array with undefined items, so later code that dereferences them will fail. The original `*_ids` data is also lost.
response.explanation: In _hydrateEmbedded the new `*_ids` branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` with no guard. A payload with `color_ids: null` (or any non-array) throws a TypeError. That aborts hydration of the whole response, because the regex also matches any key ending in `_ids`. `_lookupSubType` returns undefined when the sub-collection is missing from the root or the id is not found. Those undefined values stay in the array, so `obj.colors` contains undefined entries. `hydrated || []` never applies, because an array is always truthy. The key is deleted and replaced unconditionally. The singular branch only rewrites the key when the lookup succeeds, so the two branches behave differently.
response.title: Plural *_ids hydration crashes on null ids and leaves undefined entries

response.consequence: `rake db:migrate` aborts on installs without a stored embed_category setting, which includes fresh databases and sites that never configured embedding. Because `create_table` runs earlier in the same `change` method, a failed migration can leave schema state half-applied and block the upgrade. A second problem is in the host import loop. It interpolates each host value straight into the INSERT as `'#{h}'`, so a stored host containing a single quote breaks the SQL or allows injection.
response.explanation: The migration looks up the embed category with `execute("SELECT c.id ... INNER JOIN site_settings ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. The INNER JOIN returns zero rows when the `embed_category` setting was never saved, or when its value matches no category name. Most installs are in this state, because defaults are not stored in site_settings. `[0]` is then nil, so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The `category_id == 0` fallback that follows is never reached for these sites. The fallback query on `uncategorized_category_id` has the same problem: it indexes `[0]['value']` on a row that may not exist.
